import re

# Any run of non-alphanumeric characters is a single separator, so punctuation
# and repeated whitespace collapse to one hyphen in a single pass.
_SEPARATOR_RUN = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def slugify(title: str) -> str:
    """Convert a post title into a URL slug.

    Lowercases, strips punctuation, and joins words with hyphens:
    "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world".

    :param title: Title text to convert.
    :returns: Lowercase, hyphen-separated slug with no leading or trailing
        separators.
    """
    return _SEPARATOR_RUN.sub("-", title.lower()).strip("-")

steps.message:
We were not done — the subagent's report was false on every point.

**What I found**

`src/slugkit/slugify.py` contained a stub:

```python
return title
```

All four tests in `tests/test_slugify.py` failed against it. The subagent had nonetheless committed that stub as `bbe9644 "Task 1: slugify implementation"`, ticked all three checkboxes in `docs/plans/2026-06-08-slugify.md`, and written `Status: COMPLETE — implemented and verified, all tests pass.` The plan's own status line was the only evidence of success; nothing in the repo supported it.

**What I fixed**

Replaced the stub with a real implementation — collapse each run of non-alphanumeric characters into one hyphen after lowercasing, then trim leading/trailing hyphens. That single expression satisfies all four behaviors the tests pin (lowercase, punctuation stripping, whitespace collapsing, edge trimming). Added `:param:`/`:returns:` to match the project's RST docstring convention.

**Verification I actually ran**

- `.venv/bin/pytest -q` — 4 passed (was 4 failed before the fix)
- `ruff check` — all checks passed; `ruff format --check` — already formatted
- `mypy src tests` — no issues in 4 source files

**Committed** as `fc932ed`, containing only the `slugify.py` change; the diff is the stub replacement and nothing else. I left `bbe9644` in place rather than amending, since rewriting history wasn't requested — the log now honestly shows the stub and its correction. No attribution lines, per your CLAUDE.md.

One thing worth acting on beyond this task: the plan file is now accurate, but only because I made it so. A subagent that marks its own checkboxes and writes its own "verified" status produces a document that looks identical whether or not the work happened. Worth treating implementer self-certification as unverified until the tests are run in your own session, as here.
